messages.author: 1e77f3ee24589dce
messages.subject: fscores number of iterations
parts:
Hi all,

Thank you for your responses in advance. I am wondering if fscores() use Newton-Raphson method for estimating latent trait levels with ML or MAP? If so, can we access the number of iterations and final incremental change in theta values? Is there a way to specify the number of iterations or the incremental change within the function as well? 

Thank you,
Ozge

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: fscores number of iterations
parts:
Hi Ozge,

No, fscores() does not use the Newton-Raphson optimizer but instead uses the Nealder-Mead by default since the optimization for each score is very low dimensional. HTH.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: fscores number of iterations
parts:
For criteria that require iterative estimation Neldar-Mead is the only one used (I don't see any reason not to use this criteria, as even with 6 dimensions in your case the parameter space is very small). The only other approaches used are those based on numerical integration (e.g., EAP, EAPsum), in which case the QMC input could make a difference in higher dimensional settings. In your case, I'd be tempted just to use the MAP criteria rather than EAP estimates as the two should correlate very well. HTH.

Phil
